chapter: Growing up in the Thirteenth Ward
title: Family religion and church
summary: His family was Protestant, his mother sang in the choir at Second Baptist, and the church did not shape his music.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: My family was Protestant. But my wife, she was Catholic and her father was Methodist.
So it was like a mixture.
But when you were growing up, what church did you all attend?

Oh, we attended, my mother and father got married at Beulah Baptist Church. That's where my father was buried from, on Upper Line Street. Right. But then later on, she joined the church, that I go to now, Second Baptist, the sixth district.
Down on Laurel Street, 4218 Laurel Street is where I was.
Were your parents very religious? Did you go every Sunday?

Oh, yeah, my mother, she was. She was more religious. My father, he went. In the later years, he got back into the stream of things, but he was not active as far as doing anything. I mean, he was just a member. But my mother, she sang in the choir, you know.
Did she influence you as far as music in any way?
